R154.summary: Clement XI's Secretariat of State to the nuncio in Madrid at the opening of the War of the Quadruple Alliance. The recurring business is the promotion of Cardinal Alberoni and the settlement of the pending disputes between Rome and Spain: the nuncio's jurisdiction, the abolition of the Nunziatura in Naples, the expulsion of the nuncio, the Spanish ships bound for the Levant, the Emperor, the Turk and the peace treaty.
R154.en:
Our Lord's troubles grow on hearing that the horrid calumny is gaining ever more strength, that the Vicar of Christ was
an accomplice in the baneful wrong done by the King of Spain to Christendom and to His Holiness, and on seeing its most
pernicious effects. The expulsion of the nuncio from Naples and the total abolition of every vestige of Apostolic
authority in that kingdom has been followed by the nuncio in Vienna being forbidden access to the court and all dealings
with those ministers, with much more threatened if the Pope does not refute the said calumny with deeds. From this
little, Your Most Illustrious Lordship may gather the state in which His Holiness finds himself.

It was hoped that the piety of the King there, recognising the justice of the complaints and the fairness of His
Holiness's suggestions, would resolve to restore Sardinia and to put things back as they were;

R155.summary: Despatch 2 of the 24 in Spagna 364D from the Secretariat of State to the nuncio in Madrid, Roma 18. Genn.o? 1718; on the series, see the first entry.
R155.en:
I have several times made known to Your Most Illustrious Lordship Our Lord's regret at learning that, notwithstanding
the first chapter of the well-known Concordat, the authority and the immunity of the Church continued to be oppressed
and violated there as before; and I have also expressed to you Our Lord's astonishment at receiving from you no
account of the notorious particular outrages which the Royal Ministers were heaping up every day in this regard. But
it has never happened that I had expressly to complain of your conduct, as I am forced to do now that you are silent
to me about one of the greatest excesses that the lay power can commit against the ecclesiastical, and of which we
have, alas, authentic and irrefutable documents in hand.

R156.summary: Despatch 3 of the 24 in Spagna 364D from the Secretariat of State to the nuncio in Madrid, Roma. 8. feb.o. 1718; on the series, see the first entry.
R156.en:
I wrote to Your Most Illustrious Lordship on the 25th of last month the reasons which obliged Our Lord to suspend for
Cardinal Alberoni the grace of the translation to the Church of Seville until His Holiness should be fully satisfied
on them. Now I must inform you that Cardinal Acquaviva, to whom Our Lord took care to make known the indispensable
necessity of such a suspension, not only through me but also by himself, not showing himself satisfied with it,
claimed to move Our Lord from it by setting out his reasons, compiled in the writing of which a copy is sent to you
for no other purpose than to show there their lack of substance and the strangeness of the maxims with which His
Eminence upholds the alleged rights of the King.

R157.summary: Despatch 4 of the 24 in Spagna 364D from the Secretariat of State to the nuncio in Madrid; on the series, see the first entry.
R157.en:
... a lawful and canonical faculty. Let Your Most Illustrious Lordship therefore inform me of the truth of what has
happened in this matter, so that Our Lord may make the appropriate provisions; and meanwhile do you fulfil there those
parts which the precise obligation of the Ministry you hold will suggest to you.

R158.summary: Despatch 5 of the 24 in Spagna 364D from the Secretariat of State to the nuncio in Madrid, Roma 16 Feb.o 1718; on the series, see the first entry.
R158.en:
Your Most Illustrious Lordship will recognise from the enclosed sheets the conduct held by Cardinal Acquaviva because
Our Lord has, not refused, but merely deferred the proposal of the Church of Seville, and the steps taken by Our Lord's
ministers for the pure and simple [?preservation] of the incontestable reasons that support the Holy See and His
Holiness in this business. Three things, besides the protest, have justly increased the bitterness of Our Lord, who
hopes that they too can in no way be approved by the King.

The first appears from the sheet marked A.

R159.summary: Despatch 6 of the 24 in Spagna 364D from the Secretariat of State to the nuncio in Madrid, Roma 22. Marzo 1718; on the series, see the first entry.
R159.en:
Your Most Illustrious Lordship's last despatch, dated the 2nd of this month, which reached me with an express sent to
Cardinal Acquaviva, would require from me a very long reply; but since a new, unexpected and most grave development,
which has surprised not only Our Lord but this whole Court, obliges me to make an express despatch to you promptly, I
refer to what I shall convey to you by it by Our Lord's order.

R160.summary: Despatch 7 of the 24 in Spagna 364D from the Secretariat of State to the nuncio in Madrid, Roma. 29. Marzo. 1718; on the series, see the first entry.
R160.en:
The express which, as I indicated to Your Most Illustrious Lordship with the last despatch, was to be sent by us to
that Court has not yet left. It will leave shortly, however, and with it you will receive the answers to your
despatches of the 14th and 21st of February and of the 2nd of March.

R161.summary: Despatch 8 of the 24 in Spagna 364D from the Secretariat of State to the nuncio in Madrid, Roma. 2. Aple. 1718; on the series, see the first entry.
R161.en:
The principal aim of this despatch of ours, and the object of all Our Lord's concern, tend to turning against the
Infidels that powerful armament which Spain is preparing against Italy. If this is obtained, Your Most Illustrious
Lordship may well be persuaded that every possible facility will be found for the settlement of the other pending
matters; and the merit that Cardinal Alberoni would gain from it, to whom the principal glory would justly be
attributed, would destroy in an instant any sinister impression formed against him, and would remove all the
obstacles that keep His Holiness from continuing towards him the demonstrations of his love.

R162.summary: Despatch 9 of the 24 in Spagna 364D from the Secretariat of State to the nuncio in Madrid, Roma. 2. Aprile. 1718; on the series, see the first entry.
R162.en:
If the King persisted in the design of disturbing the peace of Christendom and of diverting the Christian arms engaged
against the Turk, and much more if the Emperor justified with authentic documents the accusation made against Spain
and Cardinal Alberoni, as His Majesty for that matter intends to do, Your Most Illustrious Lordship sees well that the
Pope could not limit himself to the mere prayers, complaints and threats made in the letters written in clear. His own
duty would oblige him to pass to deeds, and first of all to suspend the effect of those graces which the Supreme
Pontiffs his predecessors granted to the Catholic Kings for the sole and only purpose of supplying them with means
sufficient to keep the war against the Infidels alive at sea.

R163.summary: Despatch 10 of the 24 in Spagna 364D from the Secretariat of State to the nuncio in Madrid, Roma. 2. Aprile? 1718; on the series, see the first entry.
R163.en:
If the King persisted in the design of disturbing the peace of Christendom and of diverting the Christian arms engaged
against the Turk, and much more if the Emperor justified with authentic documents the accusation made against Spain
and Cardinal Alberoni, as His Majesty for that matter intends to do, Your Most Illustrious Lordship sees well that the
Pope could not limit himself to the mere prayers, complaints and threats made in the letters written in clear. His own
duty would oblige him to pass to deeds, and first of all to suspend the effect of those graces which the Supreme
Pontiffs his predecessors granted to the Catholic Kings for the sole and only purpose of supplying them with means
sufficient to keep the war against the Infidels alive at sea.

R164.summary: Despatch 11 of the 24 in Spagna 364D from the Secretariat of State to the nuncio in Madrid, Roma. 19. Aple. 1718; on the series, see the first entry.
R164.en:
The news brought me by Your Most Illustrious Lordship's cipher dated the 14th of last month, touching the present
dispositions of that Court, and principally those concerning the armament, are most important; and Our Lord desires
that you go on sending them to me as far in advance as possible, since you can well understand how much it matters to
Our Lord's good service to be informed of everything promptly. To which end let Your Most Illustrious Lordship use all
diligence and attention to find out with certainty both the designs held there and the measures it is intended to
take.

R165.summary: Despatch 12 of the 24 in Spagna 364D from the Secretariat of State to the nuncio in Madrid, Roma. 17. Mag. 1718; on the series, see the first entry.
R165.en:
It would be no great thing if, peace being concluded between the Emperor and Spain, the Catholic King took occasion to
answer, as every duty and propriety would require, the letter written to him in Our Lord's own hand, by declaring to
His Holiness that his fatherly remonstrances too had induced him to lend a hand to the conclusion of the Treaty, so
as not to hinder the progress of the Christian arms against the Turk. This is very little; and yet, besides being very
much in keeping with that distinguished piety of which the King makes [?profession], to his great praise, and not at
all unbecoming to his royal dignity, it would be taken by Our Lord as some satisfaction for the most grave failure
done to him last year, which nonetheless remains, and will always remain, deeply impressed on His Holiness's mind.

R166.summary: Despatch 13 of the 24 in Spagna 364D from the Secretariat of State to the nuncio in Madrid, Roma 31 Maj 1718; on the series, see the first entry.
R166.en:
The present despatch is sent with the express which Cardinal Acquaviva is sending there; but let Your Most Illustrious
Lordship expect very soon another, with which you will receive a Brief suspending all the Indults which that Crown
enjoys by Apostolic authority, to be executed whenever His Majesty does not refrain from diverting the Emperor from
continuing the war against the Turk. I do not repeat the reasons Our Lord has for proceeding to this step, because you
will be able to read them in my despatch of the second of April and in that of today.

R167.summary: Despatch 14 of the 24 in Spagna 364D from the Secretariat of State to the nuncio in Madrid, Roma. 31. Mag.o 1718; on the series, see the first entry.
R167.en:
There were two principal commissions which our despatch of the 2nd of April last, sent to Your Most Illustrious
Lordship by the extraordinary courier, brought you. The first, the more essential, and for every reason closest to
Our Lord's heart, concerned acting so that that Court should not only not divert, directly or indirectly, the progress
of the Christian arms against the Turk, but should moreover dispose itself to turn against him those forces which
seemed destined to harm the Emperor, I declaring to Your Most Illustrious Lordship expressly what the Pope's resolute
determination would be if the strong remonstrances you were to make on this subject had not had the desired effect.
The other concerned both the difficulties that still delayed the proposal of the Church of Seville in favour of
Cardinal Alberoni and the means proportioned to cutting them short.

R168.summary: Despatch 15 of the 24 in Spagna 364D from the Secretariat of State to the nuncio in Madrid, Dup.B, Roma. 31. Mag. 1718; on the series, see the first entry.
R168.en:
The present despatch is sent with the express which Cardinal Acquaviva is sending there; but let Your Most Illustrious
Lordship expect very soon another, with which you will receive a Brief suspending all the Indults which that Crown
enjoys by Apostolic authority, to be executed whenever His Majesty does not refrain from diverting the Emperor from
continuing the war against the Turk. I do not repeat the reasons Our Lord has for proceeding to this step, because you
will be able to read them in my despatch of the second of April and in that of today.

R169.summary: Despatch 16 of the 24 in Spagna 364D from the Secretariat of State to the nuncio in Madrid, Roma 9 Giugno 1718; on the series, see the first entry.
R169.en:
Cardinal Acquaviva, immediately after the despatch of the courier sent there on the 31st of last month, on the morning
of the first of this month had all the Spaniards called to him, notifying them by royal order that they must promptly
withdraw from Rome and refrain from making any application at the Dataria or at any other tribunal of Rome, under pain
of the royal indignation, and of resentment being taken also against the relatives of transgressors.

R170.summary: Despatch 17 of the 24 in Spagna 364D from the Secretariat of State to the nuncio in Madrid, Roma a Giugno 1718; on the series, see the first entry.
R170.en:
Following what I wrote to Your Most Illustrious Lordship under the 31st of last month by the extraordinary courier sent
to you there by Cardinal Acquaviva, I send you by this express the Brief suspending the well-known Indults granted at
other times, and then renewed from time to time by this Holy See to the Kings of Spain. The mere reading of the Brief
itself, besides all the very strong reasons [?so] amply set out to you both in my despatch of the 2nd of April last and
in the last one of the 31st of May, will serve as sufficient instruction for Your Most Illustrious Lordship, so as to
understand well that His Holiness could not excuse himself from coming promptly to such a step, and will put you in a
position to justify it also to others. I therefore think it superfluous to enlarge further on this, because I could
only repeat the same things to you.

R171.summary: Despatch 18 of the 24 in Spagna 364D from the Secretariat of State to the nuncio in Madrid, Roma. 21. Giug.o 1718; on the series, see the first entry.
R171.en:
The news which Your Most Illustrious Lordship gives touching the present public emergencies has been very welcome to Our
Lord, to whom it matters very much to be faithfully and entirely informed of everything. Do you continue, then, with
your usual attention, and as long as you are permitted, your reports, with the assurance of His Holiness's full
appreciation.

R172.summary: Despatch 19 of the 24 in Spagna 364D from the Secretariat of State to the nuncio in Madrid, Roma. 12. Luglio. 1718; on the series, see the first entry.
R172.en:
From the short despatch dated the 27th of last month, which Your Most Illustrious Lordship handed to the courier who
returned here from Lisbon, we have heard of the full execution you gave to the orders prescribed to you under the 9th of
the said month. Our Lord received the news with much satisfaction, and gave due praise to the punctuality with which
you carried them out, waiting impatiently to learn all the circumstances of it with the return of our courier. His
Holiness knows the indignation Spain will conceive at it, and all that may follow from such indignation; but, to tell
you, it matters much more to the Pope not to fall into the hands of the living God by not fulfilling his obligation in
the circumstances in which Christendom finds itself, from which men cannot free him, than to expose himself to falling
into those of men, from which the mighty hand of God can easily save him;

R173.summary: Despatch 20 of the 24 in Spagna 364D from the Secretariat of State to the nuncio in Madrid; on the series, see the first entry.
R173.en:
Before the arrival of the express that Your Most Illustrious Lordship sent back to us, Cardinal Acquaviva, following a
courier from [?that] court that had reached him earlier, had told some friend of his of the complaints being made there
because the Pope had ordered Your Most Illustrious Lordship to close the nunciature without even informing the King;
and that, although His Majesty's piety had tried to persuade you to suspend it, it had not succeeded, and that
therefore, Your Most Illustrious Lordship having been stripped of your character by His Holiness, the King had not
thought it proper to consent to your remaining any longer in his kingdoms.

His Holiness learned at once what the said Cardinal was saying;

R174.summary: Despatch 21 of the 24 in Spagna 364D from the Secretariat of State to the nuncio in Madrid, Augosto Roma 19. Lug ; 1718; on the series, see the first entry.
R174.en: ... hands of the Lord Commissary of the Cruzada the Brief on parchment, has been very wise and timely.

R175.summary: Despatch 22 of the 24 in Spagna 364D from the Secretariat of State to the nuncio in Madrid, Aug. ^10 Roma 19. Luglio 1718; on the series, see the first entry.
R175.en: ... [show]n that he has any order to discuss the present pending matters. If he does, we shall see.

R176.summary: Despatch 23 of the 24 in Spagna 364D from the Secretariat of State to the nuncio in Madrid, Roma. 19. Luglio. 1718; on the series, see the first entry.
R176.en:
Before the arrival of the express which Your Most Illustrious Lordship sent back to me, Cardinal Acquaviva, following a
courier from that Court that had reached him earlier, had told some friend of his of the complaints being made there
because the Pope had ordered Your Most Illustrious Lordship to close the Nunciature without even giving the King account
of it; and moreover that, His Majesty's piety [?having] tried to persuade you to suspend it, it had not succeeded; and
that therefore, Your Most Illustrious Lordship being stripped of your character by His Holiness, it had not seemed to
befit the King's dignity to consent that you remain any longer in his kingdoms. His Holiness learned at once what the
said Cardinal was saying;

R177.summary: Despatch 24 of the 24 in Spagna 364D from the Secretariat of State to the nuncio in Madrid, Roma 19. Luglio. 1718; on the series, see the first entry.
R177.en:
The caution Your Most Illustrious Lordship used in delivering the Brief on parchment [...] the hands of the Lord
Commissary of the Cruzada has been very wise and timely.
